authserv_explainer_summary.message: What is a trusted authentication server?

authserv_explainer_body.message: When a message arrives, your mail provider checks whether the sender is genuine (SPF, DKIM, DMARC) and writes the verdict into a hidden header. Each verdict is labelled with the name of the server that made it. Because anyone can write such a header — including spammers — this add-on only uses verdicts labelled with a server name you have confirmed. Nothing is ever trusted automatically.

authserv_explainer_advanced.message: Technical details: the header is Authentication-Results (RFC 8601) and the server name is its authserv-id. The trusted list below stores authserv-id values.
authserv_explainer_advanced.description: Raw technical terms for advanced users

rule_composite_ownDomainAuthFail_summary.message: Message claims to come from one of your account domains but authentication failed.

rule_composite_unparseableFromWithInfras.message: The From header could not be parsed as a valid address and infrastructure signals differ.

rule_composite_geoTokenCompoundDomain_su.message: The registrable domain is a hyphen-compound containing a known spam geo/token and auth is unaligned.

rule_composite_deepServiceWordSubdomain_.message: A deep subdomain contains a service-like word (e.g. mail-01) associated with disposable-domain spam.

rule_composite_dmarcFailDkimAlignedListM.message: DMARC fail mitigated: DKIM aligned and list headers present
DMARC failed but DKIM is aligned and List headers are present — likely a mailing list.

rule_composite_dkimFailWithAlignedPass_t.message: DKIM fail with aligned DKIM pass

rule_composite_dkimFailWithAlignedPass_s.message: At least one DKIM signature failed but another aligned signature passed.

rule_composite_brandDivergencePhishing_s.message: The From display name matches a well-known brand but the From domain is unrelated to that brand.

rule_composite_unsecuredDeepSubdomain_su.message: The From address uses a deep subdomain on a domain with no DMARC enforcement policy and no aligned authentication.

rule_composite_unauthenticatedFromSpoof_.message: The visible From domain has no aligned, trusted authentication and another sender identifier disagrees with it.

rule_composite_authenticatedDisplayNameS.message: Authenticated sender with spoofed display-name email
The message authenticates for its From domain but the display name contains an email address pointing to a different domain.

rule_composite_alignedAuthenticationConf.message: The visible From domain has aligned, trusted authentication with no conflicting signal.

rule_composite_publicDomainSpoofing_titl.message: Public mailbox provider domain with failed authentication

rule_composite_publicDomainSpoofing_summ.message: The visible From domain is a major public mailbox provider but authentication failed and the sending infrastructure is inconsistent.

rule_composite_spfAlignedDkimUnalignedRa.message: Spam that controls only the MAIL FROM domain to pass SPF while using throwaway local parts.

rule_composite_authAlignedRandomDomain_t.message: Attacker owns a random-string domain and uses a real ESP to get aligned auth.

rule_composite_thirdPartyAuthRandomLocal.message: Spam relayed through a third party with throwaway From addresses.

rule_composite_messageIdMismatchWithUnal.message: Forged messages often have mismatched Message-ID domains when the auth infrastructure is unrelated. Note: Forwarded or aliased mail may show a Message-ID from the original originating domain.

rule_composite_messageIdUnregistrableMis.message: A strong forgery indicator; legitimate mail always has a valid Message-ID domain.

rule_composite_fromSenderMismatchWithUna.message: Mismatch between From and Sender is a resend or impersonation pattern. Note: Mailing lists and forwarding services may set Sender to their own domain.

rule_composite_deepRandomFromSubdomain_t.message: Spam campaigns register one domain and send from many random sub-paths to evade per-domain blocking.

rule_composite_delegatedDkimAlignedRoute.message: Reduces false positives for bulk mail sent via delegated DKIM-signing ESPs.

rule_composite_spfPassDkimFailRandomLoca.message: Indicates a bulk sender relying only on SPF with throwaway local parts.

rule_composite_dkimAlignedLexicalMitigat.message: A valid aligned DKIM signature means the From domain signed the message, making random local parts less suspicious.

rule_composite_ownDomainAuthFail_tooltip.message: A high-confidence impersonation signal: your own domain should always authenticate successfully.

rule_composite_unparseableFromWithInfras.message: Malformed From headers with mismatched infrastructure are a strong forgery indicator.

rule_composite_geoTokenCompoundDomain_to.message: A common disposable-domain spam pattern using geographic or keyword tokens.

rule_composite_deepServiceWordSubdomain_.message: Spammers reuse patterns like mail-01.random-domain.tld to evade per-domain reputation.

rule_composite_dmarcFailDkimAlignedListM.message: Mailing lists often break DMARC while preserving DKIM; treating this as high-risk causes false positives.

rule_composite_dkimFailWithAlignedPass_t.message: Having both a passing and failing aligned DKIM signature is unusual and associated with message manipulation.

rule_composite_brandDivergencePhishing_t.message: A phishing sender controls an unrelated domain and authenticates it correctly, while using a famous brand name in the visible From field to deceive the recipient. Note: Official brand aliases (e.g. aexp.com for American Express) and regional brand domains not in the top-domain list may appear as mismatches.

rule_composite_unsecuredDeepSubdomain_to.message: Disposable domains often configure deep service-looking subdomains (e.g. sivakeso.support.sn5799.com) while leaving DMARC unset, evading per-label and auth-enforcement checks.

rule_composite_unauthenticatedFromSpoof_.message: Forged messages typically lack aligned authentication while carrying mismatched infrastructure headers (Message-ID, Return-Path, Reply-To) that reveal the true sending infrastructure. Note: Suppressed when the add-on's PSL-aware alignment considers auth aligned (e.g. SPF pass for example.com when From is news.example.com).

rule_composite_authenticatedDisplayNameS.message: Attackers craft display names like "user@victim.com" while sending from an authenticated but unrelated domain, deceiving users who only see the display name. Note: Legitimate mail clients and mailing lists rarely embed email addresses in display names; this pattern is almost exclusively a phishing technique.

rule_composite_alignedAuthenticationConf.message: Positive confirmation that the sender domain is properly authenticated; logged as a diagnostic signal for the decision log.

rule_composite_publicDomainSpoofing_tool.message: Legitimate messages from providers such as Outlook, iCloud, and Yahoo are always authenticated; a failed-auth message claiming to originate from these domains almost certainly has a spoofed From. Note: Suppressed when the add-on's PSL-aware alignment considers the sender authenticated (e.g. SPF pass from a subdomain of the provider domain such as bounce.mail.outlook.com).

rule_template_custom_formula_summary.message: User-defined custom scoring formula (L5 advanced feature).

notification_single_account.description: Notification title for a single new message; $account$ is the receiving account email address

notification_single_fallback.description: Notification title for a single new message when account email is unavailable; $name$ is the account display name or folder name

notification_multi_title.description: Notification title when multiple new messages are coalesced into one notification

notification_multi_body.description: First line of the notification body for multiple new messages

notification_more_messages.description: Line appended to the notification body showing how many additional messages are queued

notification_no_subject.description: Fallback shown in the notification body when the message subject is empty
